title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python toolkit for writing GPU-accelerated simulation and geometry code that can plug into robotics and machine-learning workflows. It is useful when you need fast differentiable or physics-heavy computation in Python without dropping entirely into custom CUDA infrastructure.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a lightweight sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and reinforcement learning agents without depending on ROS. It provides native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution across several common robot platforms, including Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101, making it useful for researchers who want a leaner path from simulation experiments to real robot control.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable simulation setup for building robot learning environments from interchangeable robots, objects, tasks, and scenes. It is aimed at quickly prototyping new robotic tasks and evaluating learned policies across different embodiments and environment configurations, making it useful for scaling up simulation coverage without rebuilding each setup from scratch.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: XuPeng23/AeroVLA
summary: AeroVLA is an ECCV 2026 vision-language-action model for UAV navigation that maps visual and language inputs directly to minimalist end-to-end control actions. The repository appears to provide the official implementation for training or evaluating this aerial navigation policy, with interest mainly in how far VLA-style embodied control can be simplified for drones without hand-engineered planning stacks.

extra.full_text: [Accepted to ECCV 2026] Official repository for AeroVLA (formerly known as AerialVLA): A Vision-Language-Action Model for UAV Navigation via Minimalist End-to-End Control

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for training and evaluating basic quadruped locomotion across multiple robot platforms. It is useful as a starting point for sim-to-sim and sim-to-real locomotion pipelines, packaging the environment structure needed to move policies from IsaacLab experiments toward deployment.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse
summary: RoboVerse aims to unify robot learning infrastructure by packaging a platform, dataset, and benchmark around scalable, generalizable robot behavior. It is meant to give researchers a common place to build and evaluate robot learning methods across tasks, reducing the usual fragmentation between simulation, data collection, and benchmarking.

extra.full_text: RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark for Scalable and Generalizable Robot Learning

title: wertyuilife2/go2_rl_robotlab
summary: wertyuilife2/go2_rl_robotlab appears to host code for an RSS 2026 project on robust quadrupedal locomotion for the Unitree Go2, centered on improving sim-to-real predictability with a Mixture-of-Experts policy. The interesting angle is reliability: rather than only training a stronger locomotion controller in simulation, the project targets whether MoE-based behaviors remain predictable when transferred to the real robot.
